name: Vardenafil

what.text: Vardenafil is a small-molecule drug called a PDE5 inhibitor. It was first sold in the US as Levitra, a film-coated tablet, and Staxyn, a tablet that dissolves in the mouth. Both were approved for erectile dysfunction (ED). Both brands are now discontinued in the US; generic vardenafil tablets are approved.
How it acts, according to the FDA label

items.text: During sexual stimulation, nitric oxide raises cGMP in the smooth muscle of the penis. cGMP relaxes the muscle and lets more blood flow in.
PDE5 is the most abundant enzyme that breaks cGMP down in penile tissue. Vardenafil blocks it. Sexual stimulation is needed for it to work.
Vardenafil and its main breakdown product have a half-life of about 4 to 5 hours.

research.text: Vardenafil has a large body of randomized trials. The Levitra label says film-coated and dissolving vardenafil tablets were given to more than 17,000 men in controlled and uncontrolled trials. Two published trials are listed below as they were run.
In the label's placebo-controlled trials, 2,203 men took vardenafil and 1,199 took placebo. The largest North American fixed-dose trial evaluated 762 men, mean age 57.

research.title: Erectile dysfunction, first at-home trial (IJIR 2001)

facts.v: Porst H, Rosen R, Padma-Nathan H, et al. Int J Impot Res 2001;13(4):192-9
601 men with mild to severe ED; 580 in the main analysis
IIEF questions 3 (penetration) and 4 (keeping an erection); all IIEF domains; a global question

research.found: Scores on both questions rose more on all three doses than on placebo (P<0.001). 71% to 75% of intercourse attempts were successful across doses. On 20 mg, 80% reported improved erections vs 30% on placebo. Headache (7% to 15%), flushing (10% to 11%), and indigestion or stuffy nose (up to 7%) were most frequent.

src.label: Porst et al., Int J Impot Res, PubMed

research.title: Erectile dysfunction in men with diabetes (Diabetes Care 2003)

facts.v: Goldstein I, Young JM, Fischer J, et al. Diabetes Care 2003;26(3):777-83
multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose, parallel-group Phase III
452 men with type 1 or type 2 diabetes and ED
vardenafil 10 or 20 mg or placebo, as needed
IIEF domain scores, rates of penetration and successful intercourse, a global question

research.found: 57% (10 mg) and 72% (20 mg) reported improved erections vs 13% on placebo (P<0.0001). Final IIEF erectile function scores were 17.1 and 19.0 vs 12.6 on placebo. Side effects were mainly mild to moderate headache (up to 13%), flushing (up to 10%) and stuffy nose (up to 10%).

src.label: Goldstein et al., Diabetes Care, PubMed

us.text: Vardenafil is FDA approved, by prescription, for erectile dysfunction. The Levitra (2003) and Staxyn (2010) brands are discontinued, and FDA found they were not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons. Generic vardenafil tablets are approved. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: film-coated tablets approved August 19, 2003 (NDA 021400) for erectile dysfunction. All strengths are now listed as discontinued, with a Federal Register determination that they were not discontinued for safety or effectiveness reasons.

an orally disintegrating tablet approved June 17, 2010 (NDA 200179) for erectile dysfunction, now discontinued with the same determination. Its label says it is not interchangeable with Levitra because it gives higher levels of the drug in the body.
for example, Teva's generic vardenafil tablets were approved May 3, 2012 (ANDA 091347) and are listed as prescription products.
the label says vardenafil must not be used with nitrates or nitric oxide donors in any form, or with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat.
the Levitra label says combinations with other ED treatments have not been studied and are not recommended.

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. If the vardenafil tablet Adonis carries is compounded, it is not an FDA-approved product.
FDA says compounded drugs are not FDA approved, which means FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are marketed.

world.lead: Vardenafil is an approved prescription medicine in the US (now as generics) and in the EU (Levitra). Its status in the UK, Canada and Australia is still being confirmed with each regulator's own product record. It is not on WADA's Prohibited List.

after.text: Australia: vardenafil is listed in Schedule 4 (prescription-only) of the October 2026 Poisons Standard. TGA's product information search returned no vardenafil documents when checked.

Canada: a 2018 Health Canada advisory on seized sexual-enhancement products described vardenafil as a prescription drug for ED, to be used only under a health care professional's supervision and never with nitrate drugs.
United Kingdom: MHRA reported in February 2026 that illegally sold ED pills it seized contained sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil and avanafil.

after.text: Vardenafil is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is not in the 2027 Monitoring Program either. Class S0 covers only substances with no government approval for human use, and vardenafil is approved (see above).

side.text: The label lists headache, flushing and stuffy nose as the most common side effects. Serious risks include a dangerous drop in blood pressure with nitrates, erections lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision loss, sudden hearing loss and changes in heart rhythm (QT prolongation).

items.text: headache (15% on vardenafil vs 4% on placebo), flushing (11% vs 1%), stuffy or runny nose (9% vs 3%), indigestion (4% vs 1%), sinusitis and flu-like symptoms (3% each), dizziness, raised creatine kinase and nausea (2% each). Some rose with dose.
men should not use it if sex is inadvisable because of their heart condition.

in a study of 59 healthy men, vardenafil raised the QTc interval about as much as the antibiotic moxifloxacin. Men with congenital QT prolongation or taking Class IA or III antiarrhythmic drugs should avoid it.
an erection lasting more than 4 hours needs immediate medical help.
can be a sign of NAION, a type of optic nerve damage. The label tells patients to stop and seek care.
the label tells patients to stop and seek care if hearing suddenly drops or is lost.

items.lead: Low blood pressure with other drugs:
items.text: alpha-blockers can lower blood pressure significantly with vardenafil, sometimes causing fainting. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ritonavir or ketoconazole raise vardenafil levels.
the label says not to use it in severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh C) or in men on kidney dialysis.
each tablet contained phenylalanine, which can harm people with phenylketonuria.

surprises: Levitra is often named as a current brand, but FDA lists Levitra and Staxyn as discontinued in the US (not for safety or effectiveness reasons); vardenafil is now sold there as generics.
FDA's Staxyn label says a mouth-dissolving vardenafil tablet is not interchangeable with the swallowed tablet because it gives higher drug levels: a change in form changed exposure.
